common_name: Cool Glow Pomegranate Nandina (Lacy Red-Winter Heavenly Bamboo)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun to partial shade; Cool Glow Pomegranate holds its dense, rounded mound shape with little pruning.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this First Editions introduction carries finely cut, lacy dark-green foliage through spring and summer before switching to a strong pomegranate-red winter color that is more saturated than the muted bronze many older nandinas show in cold weather. Small white flower clusters appear in late spring, and the plant builds into a dense, upright, rounded mound without the legginess some larger nandina cultivars develop. It tolerates a wide range of soils and dry spells once established and needs only light shaping to stay tidy in foundation plantings or mixed borders. Give it a few hours of direct sun for the best winter foliage saturation.

common_name: Cool Glow Lime Nandina (Bright Lime-Green Heavenly Bamboo)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil and give at least 6 hours of direct sun daily; Cool Glow Lime needs strong light to develop its signature lime-green to gold foliage tone.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to light partial shade, aiming for at least six hours of direct sun daily to bring out the strongest foliage color. This First Editions companion to Cool Glow Pomegranate carries bright lime-green to chartreuse-gold foliage year-round rather than the typical dark-green-to-red seasonal shift of most nandinas, giving it a distinctly brighter presence in the landscape. It forms a compact, dense, rounded mound, sets relatively few berries, and is seldom browsed by deer. Once established it tolerates drought and a wide range of soil types, making it a low-fuss choice for brightening foundation plantings or mixed borders where a chartreuse accent is wanted.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Goldstream stays compact and narrow-leaved without the shearing some nandinas need to control size.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; introduced by Sidhu & Sons Nursery, Goldstream is distinguished by narrow, finely dissected foliage with a lacier texture than most nandina cultivars. New growth flushes yellow to gold in spring, settling toward green in summer before deepening into a rich amber-gold winter color, and small white flowers appear in late spring. Its compact, naturally tidy habit of roughly three feet tall and wide suits foundation plantings and mixed borders without routine pruning. Like other nandinas it tolerates heat, a range of soil types, and short dry spells once established.

common_name: Snow Dance Loropetalum (White-Flowered Arching Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade with regular water through the first season; Snow Dance grows considerably larger than most compact loropetalum cultivars and needs room for its arching branches.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, giving it room to spread since mature plants reach six to eight feet in both directions on gracefully arching branches. Unlike the pink- and red-flowered loropetalum cultivars that dominate the market, Snow Dance bears masses of white, spidery, fringe-like flowers, mainly in a heavy spring flush with scattered rebloom through the growing season. New leaves emerge reddish before aging to a light olive-green, giving a softer two-tone look to the foliage than the burgundy-leaved cultivars. In colder parts of its range the plant can go semi-deciduous for winter, and regular water during establishment helps it fill in as a loose hedge, screen, or background shrub.
